newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Market not seen in long retreat.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Market not seen in long retreat.

text.p: Investors in major U.S. stock indices focused on puts Wednesday as the market suffered its first major correction after rallying to record highs earlier this week, traders said.
The action did not suggest the market was poised to enter a longer term consolidation, said Jay Shartsis, head of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co in New York.
"To stop the whole rally, you probably need an extended period of call buying and you really haven't seen that," Shartsis said.
At 1430 CDT/1930 GMT, put volume in the S&P 100 index outpaced call volume by 73,793 to 60,708. Among S&P 500 index .SPX options, put volume led call volume 67,360 to 23,337.
The Dow industrial average was at its session lows, down 123 points at 7,102. The blue chip barometer closed at a record high 7,225 on Tuesday.
The SPX fell 10-1/2 points to 817.25 and the OEX lost 10.3 points to 801.23.
June S&P 500 futures were off 15.35 at 819, their session low. The hit a new contract high of 838 on Monday.
"Options indicators are about neutral," Shartsis said. "So after a quick drop here they'll probably come up and try the highs again."
With the market maintaining its wildly choppy tone of late, volatility rose, traders said.
"The volatility's still way up," one trader said. He noted that volatility in the OEX held firm Tuesday as June S&P futures moved lower despite the Dow's gains.
The Chicago Board Options Exchange's volatility index, priced off certain OEX options, was up 0.36, or 1.62 percent, at 22.60.
In the OEX, action was led by the May 810 call, which traded more than 14,900 contracts. The option, which had open interest of 12,013 through Tuesday, fell 8-5/8 to 5-7/8.
Other busy OEX calls included the May 815, the May 820 and the May 805.
On the put side, the May 800 was most active, with turnover of nearly 9,100 contracts. The May 770, 805 and 810 puts were also active.
Trading in the OEX dropped off sharply after the May series.
